clue.text: Means of preserving food adapted from a steam iron

indicators.note: something adapted is altered, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone improvises a food store out of an old steam iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges A STEAM into MEATSA; 'from' joins it to FE, the symbol for iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat safe is a ventilated cupboard for keeping food cool and away from flies, a pre-fridge larder.

clue.text: Native ruler has a glass of beer and a bit of meat sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the whole run of letters is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer
ham is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: An Indian prince enjoys a pint and a slice of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns the whole run A JAR A HAM backwards. 'Jar' for a drink is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja was the hereditary prince of an Indian state, a native ruler under the Raj.

clue.text: Wisely, fashionable lady goes round dives in disguise

indicators.note: one set of letters goes round the other
to fashion is to shape, so these letters are reshaped
something in disguise has its appearance changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stylish woman disguises herself to tour seedy bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges LADY into ADLY; 'in disguise' rearranges DIVES into DVISE; 'goes round' puts DVISE inside ADLY after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something advisedly means doing it deliberately and after careful thought, which is acting with prudence.

clue.text: Wild ass in India? No, blackbuck

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
N is the abbreviation for number, written No

explanation.surface: Asking whether a wild ass lives in India, and being told it is actually an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges ASS into SAS; 'in' is a link. The OCR had a stray '6' not on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackbuck is an Indian antelope, also known by a Hindi-derived name.

clue.text: General's boy can perhaps run about

indicators.note: one word is placed about, that is around, the other

parts.note: to run away is to flee

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may be in another order

explanation.surface: A soldier's son is good for running errands, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CAN into ANC; 'about' wraps FLEE round it. The general is Banquo in Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Macbeth, the general Banquo has a son who escapes the murderers sent for them both.

clue.text: The inane brain-child?

parts.note: read as 'The in ane': ANE is the Scots word for one, and THE goes inside it

explanation.surface: A mocking question asking whether some foolish idea is the brain-child of an empty head.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'inane' as 'in ane': ANE is Scots for 'one', so the clue says put THE inside ANE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the goddess of wisdom sprang fully armed from the head of Zeus, literally a child of his brain.

clue.text: Self-announcement of one on the line to furious woman

parts.note: 'Tis I' is an old-fashioned way to announce yourself
someone on the line is on the telephone

explanation.surface: A caller announces themselves to an angry woman down the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as ''Tis I' on the phone, with 'of one' a link. 'furious' points to the Furies of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: She is one of the three Furies, the avenging goddesses of Greek myth, the one who punished murder.

clue.text: Remove to period quarters

parts.note: an era is a period of history
S and E are two of the four compass quarters, south and east

explanation.surface: An order to remove someone to their living quarters for a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' are compass points, not lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or delete, so take away completely.

clue.text: The 'centre of Odessa has come down in value

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here two from a six-letter word

parts.note: rain that comes down heavily is said to teem

explanation.surface: The middle of a Black Sea port has fallen in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the middle pair of ODESSA; 'The' and 'has' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to regard highly, prize or rate, so to hold something dear.

clue.text: Preliminary puff for these African summers

explanation.surface: An introductory blurb about some African people who add up figures.
explanation.walkthrough: The puff is the word 'puff' placed before: the puff adder is an African viper. 'summers' means people who do sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Puff precedes the snake's name in an African viper; and those who add up figures do sums.

clue.text: Breeding places for urticaria

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding note about where a skin rash breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees breed in their wooden homes, and a nettle-rash skin complaint (urticaria) has the same common name.

clue.text: She removes garments to make the cases tidy

indicators.note: the letters of the words are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman takes clothes out of suitcases to keep them neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' signals rearranging CASES TIDY; 'the' is a link. The surface suggests unpacking, not undressing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease artist, a word coined by H. L. Mencken from the Greek for shedding skin.

clue.text: Jade found in Spanish work

parts.note: jade here is a worn-out horse, and the Spanish work is Cervantes's Don Quixote, whose hero rides a famous nag

explanation.surface: A green gemstone turns up in some Spanish artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jade' looks like the gemstone but is an old word for a broken-down horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote's bony old nag is named in the novel, so it is the jade of that Spanish work.

clue.text: Young conscript once losing his head to a shepherdess

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an ephebe was a young man in ancient Greece undergoing military training

explanation.surface: A young recruit of olden days is beheaded and replaced by a shepherdess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' drops the first E of EPHEBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scornful shepherdess in Shakespeare's As You Like It bears this name.

clue.text: A man may be touched, if not moved, by these words

definitions.text: A man may be touched, if not moved, by these words

parts.words: A man may be touched, if not moved, by these words
parts.note: the man is a chess piece: a player who straightens a piece without intending to move it says a French phrase meaning 'I adjust'

explanation.surface: Someone might be emotionally touched, though not deeply moved, by a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chessman, and 'touched' and 'moved' are physical, not emotional. Under the touch-move rule, the phrase excuses the touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess players say the French phrase for 'I adjust' when straightening a piece, so the touch does not oblige a move.

clue.text: Stuff into more expensive leather case

parts.note: prices that go up become more expensive
a holster is a leather case for a pistol

explanation.surface: Putting things into a pricier leather bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to pad and cover furniture, filling a chair with stuffing.

clue.text: Cloth looks peculiar in light

indicators.note: one word is put inside the other

parts.note: light, meaning short of the full amount, is shy, as in 'two shy of a dozen'
peculiar means odd

explanation.surface: Some fabric looks strange in a certain light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks' links definition and wordplay. 'light' here means lacking, as in 'shy of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy is a cheap fabric made from shredded and respun woollen rags, which is why the word also means poor quality.

clue.text: Three-halfpenny piece also grabbed by pickpocket, the despicable fellow

indicators.note: one word is grabbed and held inside the other

parts.note: a dip is slang for a pickpocket
and means also
a rat is a despicable person

explanation.surface: A small coin and more is snatched by a thief, the rotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbed by' puts AND inside DIP; 'the' is a link. The word also means a contemptible little person.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old small coin worth three halfpence, minted in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Author is said to be a Cockney in private life

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken aloud, in a Cockney accent

parts.note: taken as written, then spoken

explanation.surface: A writer is reported to be a Londoner when off duty.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kipling's Soldiers Three, one of the three privates is a Cockney; 'private' means a private soldier, not a personal life.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's Cockney soldier in Soldiers Three is a private in the ranks, hence a Cockney in private life.

clue.text: The code of A Woman of No Importance?

explanation.surface: A question about the hidden code in an Oscar Wilde play.
explanation.walkthrough: A Woman of No Importance is a play by Oscar Wilde, but here it describes a person who counts for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a secret writing system, and also a nonentity, a nobody who counts as zero.

clue.text: Drama of the old city under his initial leadership

definitions.text: Drama of the old city under his initial leadership

parts.words: Drama of the old city under his initial leadership
parts.note: the play R.U.R. is spelt as an R heading UR, the ancient city; that R is the first letter of the inventor's name

explanation.surface: A play about an ancient city ruled by its founding leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Karel Capek's play R.U.R. stands for this man's Universal Robots: his initial R sits above UR, the ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: In Capek's play the robot factory belongs to this man, whose initial begins the title.

clue.text: Not so blue as a detergent

explanation.surface: Comparing how much a washing powder whitens rather than leaves things blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Less smutty (blue meaning rude) is one sense; the other is a cleaning agent, such as a detergent.

clue.text: What the hooker can do with the ball

definitions.text: What the hooker can do with the ball

parts.words: What the hooker can do with the ball
parts.note: the hooker is someone with a hook needle, and the ball is a ball of wool or thread, not a rugby player with a ball

explanation.surface: A rugby hooker's skills with the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the hooker hooks the ball in the scrum, but here the hooker uses a hooked needle on a ball of yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: This craft makes fabric by looping yarn with a hooked needle, worked from a ball of wool.

clue.text: Ludicrous descent from the Black Mountain

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Athos is the holy mountain in northern Greece

explanation.surface: A comic fall down the side of a dark mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the' are link words. Mount Athos is home to Orthodox monasteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is an anticlimax, a sudden drop from the elevated to the trivial in writing.

clue.text: Hammer head lost by Russian craftsmen's guild

indicators.note: the head is the first letter, which is removed from the word

parts.note: a martel is a medieval war hammer

explanation.surface: A Russian guild of craftsmen loses the head of its hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head lost' drops the M from MARTEL; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An artel is a co-operative association of workers or craftsmen in Russia.

clue.text: Settle up about times and charges

indicators.note: the word placed about another goes around it
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to seat someone is to settle them
X is the multiplication sign for times

explanation.surface: Someone pays up several times over for their bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SEAT into TAES; 'about' puts it round X. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxes are levies imposed by government, compulsory payments like duties and fees.

clue.text: Dried cod for making bouillabaisse?

parts.note: a bouillabaisse is made from a stock base
the other ingredient of bouillabaisse is seafood

explanation.surface: Asking whether dried cod is what you use to make a Provencal fish stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouillabaisse is a Provencal soup, made by simmering seafood in a broth, so it supplies both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod or similar white fish split and air-dried hard without salt goes by this name.

clue.text: Where the part played by perestroika bulks large?

indicators.note: the answer is a part of these words, played out across their join

explanation.surface: Asking where the Soviet reform programme looms largest.
explanation.walkthrough: Gorbachev's perestroika coincided with the Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan, whose capital is the answer; 'the' and 'large' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Afghanistan is a place, so it answers a 'where' question.

clue.text: Judges' precedents in book form

parts.note: Judges is a book of the Bible; what precede it are the six books from Genesis to Joshua, gathered as one volume

explanation.surface: Legal precedents set by judges, collected in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests case law, but Judges is the seventh book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the first six books of the Old Testament, Genesis to Joshua, which come before Judges.

clue.text: Mineral aggregate carried by rail to the driller

indicators.note: one word is carried inside the other

parts.note: BR is short for British Rail, the former national railway
ore is a mineral aggregate from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Ore is taken by rail to a drilling site.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stood for British Rail, Britain's national railway until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or creature that makes holes is one that drills.

clue.text: Gaol is said to have killed him

definitions.text: Gaol is said to have killed him

parts.words: Gaol is said to have killed him
parts.note: spoken aloud, the prison word gives Jael, the Old Testament woman who drove a tent peg through a Canaanite general's head

explanation.surface: A man is said to have died in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaol, the British spelling of jail, sounds like Jael, who killed the commander in Judges 4.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Judges, the Canaanite captain fled to Jael's tent and was killed there while asleep.

clue.text: They were above the pillars of the religious community

definitions.text: They were above the pillars of the religious community

parts.words: They were above the pillars of the religious community
parts.note: the pillars are literal columns: certain early Christian ascetics lived on top of them

explanation.surface: Some people ranked higher than the leading figures of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pillars of the community' suggests leading citizens, but here these hermits literally lived on top of pillars.
explanation.definitionFit: Early Christian ascetics such as Simeon lived atop columns for years, so they were literally above pillars.
